subject.title: fix(agents): bound stalled SSH directory uploads with an idle watchdog

question: Should SSH sandbox directory uploads fail by default after 30 seconds with no tar-stream progress, rather than retain the current unbounded wait?
rationale: The patch is mechanically sound and proof-positive, but the default intentionally changes failure behavior for existing SSH sandbox deployments and the timeout is not a user-facing configuration setting.

options.title: Accept the bounded default
options.body: Confirm that failing a zero-progress upload after 30 seconds is preferable to an unbounded sandbox setup hang and merge the current watchdog design.

options.title: Choose a different compatibility policy
options.body: Set a different owner-approved timeout or expose a supported configuration path if deployed SSH environments need a longer no-progress allowance.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded default
recommendation.body: Confirm that failing a zero-progress upload after 30 seconds is preferable to an unbounded sandbox setup hang and merge the current watchdog design.

likelyOwner.reason: cxbAsDev introduced the adjacent SSH pipeline lifecycle behavior and is the strongest history-based routing candidate for the timeout boundary.
